D007-D005_h001.question:
I’ve been struggling for about half a year, maybe a bit more, with things not feeling real—like I’m watching my life from outside. Lately, I’ll see figures in the back seat of my cab, clear as anyone, but when I turn, no one’s there. Sometimes it’s my ex-wife, even though we’ve been divorced for years. I know it doesn’t make sense, but I *know* she’s been seeing someone else. I see them together—just out of the corner of my eye, in doorways or passing cars.  

My sleep’s been awful. I’ll lie down for eight hours and wake up like I’ve been up all night. My hands won’t stay still, I pace, rub at my arms like I’m trying to scratch something out. I used to take pride in my work—keeping the car clean, knowing the city—but now, I don’t care. Finished fares, praise, doesn’t register. It’s like everything’s wrapped in cotton.  

People ask me questions, and I start talking about one thing, then it leads elsewhere. I lose the point, I know. My dispatcher yelled at me last week—said I didn’t answer his call, just went on about traffic patterns in a neighborhood I don’t even drive.  

I can’t tell if it’s the stress, the loneliness, or if my mind’s breaking. The sadness isn’t strong—it’s more like nothing matters, nothing touches me. And those visions? They don’t scare me. They just *are*.
D007-D005_h001.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Body Dysmorphic Disorder
    D. Persistent Depressive Disorder
D007-D005_h001.answer: B & A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type) & Schizophrenia

D007-D005_h002.question:
I’ve been struggling for a while now—about seven months, maybe a little more. Most days, I feel this heavy sadness that doesn’t go away, like I’m moving through mud. Getting out of bed takes everything. I used to keep up with clients, return calls quickly, but now I barely make it to work most days, and when I do, I just sit there. My steps feel slow, even picking up the phone is hard. I’ve stopped seeing friends, even my daughter says I don’t call like I used to.

And then there are the feelings… things aren’t real anymore. I keep thinking the world is ending—like the air itself is rotting, and soon nothing will be left. Sometimes I feel bugs crawling under my skin, especially at night. Last week, I swore I felt fingers on my back, but no one was there. It happens all the time now.

I try to explain how I feel, but words don’t work right. I’ll say things like “the grint is spreading”—I know it doesn’t make sense to others, but it does to me. I don’t sleep well either. I lie there for hours, afraid to close my eyes. I don’t know how much longer I can keep doing this.
D007-D005_h002.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Body Dysmorphic Disorder
    D. Persistent Depressive Disorder
D007-D005_h002.answer: B & A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type) & Schizophrenia

D007-D005_h003.question:
I’ve been struggling for a while now—about seven months, maybe a bit more. Some days, I just feel so heavy, like I can’t get out of bed even after sleeping eight hours. I don’t enjoy things I used to—my garden, my books, nothing. My speech gets slow, I know, because my coworkers at the pharmacy ask if I’m okay. It takes me a while to answer sometimes.  

But it’s not just the sadness. There’s more. I keep smelling cigarette smoke when no one’s smoking—sometimes it’s rotten, like burnt plastic. And… I know it sounds strange, but I’m certain Dr. Langston from the clinic, the cardiologist, he’s been sending me signs. Little smiles, adjusting his coat when I walk by. He doesn’t say anything, but I know—he feels it too. We’re meant to be.  

I catch myself rhyming when I talk, even with patients. “Take two tabs, don’t be a jab—just relax with a wax,” I said the other day. I didn’t mean to. It just… slips out.  

I don’t know what’s real anymore. But I can’t stop thinking about him. I write him letters I never send. The smell comes again when I read them.  

Work’s getting harder—people notice. But I don’t know if it’s the sadness or the voices—or both.
D007-D005_h003.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Body Dysmorphic Disorder
    D. Persistent Depressive Disorder
D007-D005_h003.answer: B & A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type) & Schizophrenia

D007-D005_h004.question:
I’ve been struggling for a while now—more than half a year, maybe close to a year. Lately, I’ll be at work in the ER and suddenly smell something burning, like flesh, but no one else does. I know it doesn’t make sense, but it feels so real. I’ve started worrying there’s something seriously wrong inside me—like my liver is rotting or my blood is poisoned. The doctors run tests, and everything comes back normal, but I can’t shake the feeling.  

Sleep’s been impossible. I wake up around 3 a.m. every night and just stay that way, pacing, pulling at my cuticles until they bleed. I used to love painting, going out with friends, even just watching movies, but now nothing feels like it matters. I cry a lot—sometimes for no reason—and other times, my thoughts just… jump. I’ll be talking to a patient about their chest pain and suddenly say something about my shoes or the weather, and I don’t know how I got there.  

It’s hard to focus at work. I’m making little mistakes, forgetting meds. I still show up, but I’m not the nurse I used to be. The sadness and the weird thoughts have both been going on for so long, overlapping in a way I can’t untangle.
D007-D005_h004.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Body Dysmorphic Disorder
    D. Persistent Depressive Disorder
D007-D005_h004.answer: B & A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type) & Schizophrenia

D007-D005_h005.question:
I’ve been feeling off for about the last six or seven months—maybe longer. Things at work have gotten hard; I’m a welder, been doing it twenty years, but now I just move slow, like my arms don’t want to listen some days. I used to love coming home to my wife, but now… nothing feels good, really. I sleep a lot—sometimes I’ll wake up, watch TV for a minute, then go back under the covers till noon. 

There’s this woman I see sometimes—she’s not real, I know that sounds crazy, but she stands in the corner of my shop when I’m working. Wears a red dress. She doesn’t speak, just watches. I don’t know why she’s there. But then… I think she’s trying to tell me something important, like she cares. I found myself writing her notes, even though I don’t know her. I think she’s been sending me signs—small things, like a song on the radio or the way the sparks fly. 

I start talking about her, and my wife gets upset. I’ll say something about the job, then jump to the color red, then remember something from high school—my thoughts don’t always line up. I used to be steady. Now I feel like I’m fading.
D007-D005_h005.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Body Dysmorphic Disorder
    D. Persistent Depressive Disorder
D007-D005_h005.answer: B & A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type) & Schizophrenia

D007-D005_h006.question:
I’ve been feeling… hollow, for so long now—over a year, maybe closer to two. I don’t get pleasure from anything—not visiting friends, not even my garden, which used to bring me so much joy. Food tastes like nothing, or worse—sometimes I’ll be sitting at the table and suddenly it’s bitter, like I’m chewing on metal or ash, even if the plate’s untouched. The doctor says there’s nothing wrong with my tongue, but I *know* what I taste.  

I can’t shake the feeling that everything is unraveling. Not just me—*everything*. The world’s rotting from the inside. I dreamt the other day that the rivers had turned to poison, and when I woke up, I could still taste it. I think… I think it’s my fault somehow. Like maybe I didn’t do enough—when my husband passed, when the shelter closed down, all of it. Maybe I should’ve kept working more, done better.  

My mind jumps around sometimes—I start talking about the soup I made last week and end up worrying about wildfires in California. I don’t know how to stop it. I used to help at the food pantry twice a week, but I can’t bring myself to go anymore. What’s the point, really, if it’s all going to vanish soon anyway?
D007-D005_h006.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    D. Body Dysmorphic Disorder
D007-D005_h006.answer: A & B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type) & Schizophrenia

D007-D005_h007.question:
I’ve been struggling for over a year—maybe a year and a half now. At work, things started slipping. I’m an IT auditor, so precision matters, but I’d stare at reports and feel… hollow. Not sad, exactly—just nothing. Like I was watching my life from behind glass. I stopped meeting friends. What’s the point? I’ve lost about ten pounds without trying; food just doesn’t interest me.  

There are times I see figures near the office server room, like people in dark suits watching me, even when I know no one’s there. I can’t shake the feeling that my data is being accessed—someone’s tracking every keystroke. I know it sounds strange, but I *see* them. Once, I saw my own face on a monitor in the reflection—only it wasn’t me.  

I replay disasters—like the hospital fire last winter—and become certain I caused it, that I failed some audit that led to it. It doesn’t make sense logically, but the guilt won’t leave. My thoughts drift when people ask questions. I start answering one thing and end up somewhere else entirely. They’ve noticed. I can tell.  

I don’t know what’s real anymore. But I can’t prove they’re watching. And I can’t prove they’re not.
D007-D005_h007.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    D. Body Dysmorphic Disorder
D007-D005_h007.answer: A & B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type) & Schizophrenia

D007-D005_h008.question:
I’ve been struggling for over a year now—maybe closer to a year and a half. Things at work have gotten hard; reading the teleprompter feels like swimming through fog. I used to love anchoring—connecting with people through the screen—but now I just feel… hollow. Like there’s no spark left. I don’t even watch the shows I used to record, don’t go out, don’t care. I’ve gained weight—popped a button on my favorite suit last month—though I’m not eating more. If anything, I forget to eat.

Lately, I keep feeling things—like something’s crawling under my skin, especially during live shots. No one else feels it. And I know this sounds strange, but I can’t shake the feeling that people are talking about me on air, even when they’re not. A weatherman’s joke? A producer’s sigh? It’s all coded messages—meant for me. I even think I’m being punished somehow. That plane crash last winter—terrible, senseless—but I can’t help but believe I could’ve stopped it. Something I didn’t say. Should’ve said.

My thoughts? They jump around. I lose the thread. My director’s noticed. I know I’m slipping—but I can’t get a grip.
D007-D005_h008.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    D. Body Dysmorphic Disorder
D007-D005_h008.answer: A & B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type) & Schizophrenia

D007-D005_h009.question:
I’ve been struggling for over a year now—maybe closer to a year and a half, I don’t track it exactly. At work, things feel… off. I’m the supervisor, so I should be in control, but I can’t shake the feeling that the higher-ups are watching me through the security cameras, even when I’m off the clock. It’s not just paranoia—I *feel* them. Like something’s crawling under my skin, especially at night. I’ve checked the sheets, the mattress, even had an exterminator out. Nothing. But I still feel movement, like bugs are under the surface.  

Talking to people has gotten harder. My wife says I go off on tangents—start talking about production quotas and end up shouting about government tracking chips. I don’t mean to. My mind just… jumps.  

I don’t feel much anymore. I used to love fixing bikes with my son, but now it’s like everything’s muffled. I’ve gained weight—clothes don’t fit, not from comfort eating, just… no energy to move. And sometimes, I think my team’s injuries at work are my fault, even when I wasn’t there. Like my thoughts caused it.  

I can’t tell if the sadness came first or the voices. It’s all blurred together now.
D007-D005_h009.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    D. Body Dysmorphic Disorder
D007-D005_h009.answer: A & B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type) & Schizophrenia

D007-D005_h010.question:
I’ve been feeling off for over a year now—maybe closer to a year and a half. Things just don’t feel real sometimes. I work outside most days, planting, pruning, trying to stay busy, but my mind keeps snagging on little things. People walking by, a radio playing in a car—I can’t help but think they’re sending me messages. Not directly, but in code. Like the way someone ties their shoe or says “good morning” in a certain tone. I know it sounds strange, but it feels *true*.

And there’s this smell—burnt plastic, almost, like wires overheating. It comes out of nowhere, even when there’s nothing burning. I’ll be kneeling in the soil and suddenly catch it in my nose, strong and sour. It makes me nauseous, but no one else ever notices.

I don’t care much about work anymore. Got praised last season for redesigning a garden, but it didn’t mean anything. I used to take pride in that. Now I eat more than I should, even when I’m not hungry—just to fill something, though nothing feels full. I just feel… hollow. Like I’m fading out. Sometimes I wonder if I even matter at all. I try to talk about it, but I end up drifting off-topic, even to myself.
D007-D005_h010.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    D. Body Dysmorphic Disorder
D007-D005_h010.answer: A & B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type) & Schizophrenia

D007-D005_h011.question:
I’ve been falling apart for about seven months now. Work used to be manageable—coordinating hires, handling conflicts—but lately, I can’t focus. I hear voices, mostly at night, whispering that everything’s going to crumble—society, the planet, my family. Sometimes they say I’ve already ruined everything, that I’m a failure as a wife, as a person. I don’t know if they’re real, but they feel like truth.  

I don’t see friends anymore. I cancel plans, even birthdays. The thought of small talk exhausts me. I pace around the house, wringing my hands, can’t sit still even when I’m drained. I don’t enjoy anything—not reading, not dinner with my husband, nothing. I feel… hollow.  

I’ve started doing odd things—like bowing to the coffee machine or arranging pills in perfect rows. I don’t know why, but it feels necessary. My thoughts get tangled; I’ll start a sentence at work and lose it halfway, words spilling out that don’t connect. My team noticed.  

I think often, “I’d be better off gone.” No plan, just… relief in the idea. But is this all because I’m depressed? Or is my mind breaking in ways deeper than sadness? I can’t tell what’s real anymore—for months, it’s been this blur of voices, dread, and silence.
D007-D005_h011.options:
A. Anorexia Nervosa
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    D. Schizophrenia
D007-D005_h011.answer: B & D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type) & Schizophrenia

D007-D005_h012.question:
I’ve been struggling for about seven months now—started subtle, then worsened. At first, it was just the smell—burning hair, constantly, though no one else smells it. Then came the thoughts: I’m certain something terrible’s coming, like a firestorm that’ll wipe everything out. No use fighting it; the world’s already over, I just think I’m still in it. I catch myself saying things that don’t make sense—even to me—and lately, I repeat the same phrases under my breath, over and over, like locking the door, checking the radio. My wife says I barely talk anymore, and when I do, it’s slow. That matches how I move—like every motion takes effort. Walking feels heavy. Picking up my gear? Some days, I just stare at it. 

I don’t feel anything anymore—not joy, not love, not pride. Like the switch flipped off. I keep imagining driving out to the old reservoir at night, leaving the car running in the garage. I’ve got the plan down. No value in me, not as a cop, not as a husband. But here’s the thing—I can’t say the dark moods are *always* there. Some days, the weight lifts slightly, but the smells, the delusions—they never really leave.
D007-D005_h012.options:
A. Anorexia Nervosa
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    D. Schizophrenia
D007-D005_h012.answer: B & D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type) & Schizophrenia

D007-D005_h013.question:
I’ve been off for about seven months now—maybe longer, it’s hard to tell. Things at work started slipping; I design spaces for clients, but I couldn’t concentrate on layouts or fabrics anymore. I kept feeling bugs crawling under my skin, like something was burrowing in my arms or back, but no one else could see it. Doctors found nothing, but I *know* something’s wrong inside—my organs feel misshapen, like they’ve shifted.  

I catch myself saying things that don’t make sense, like “The light’s too bright, so I’ll take flight with the kite”—it just pops out, rhyming like that. I’ve paced my living room the same way every night, tracing the tiles over and over. My husband says I’ve changed—don’t answer when friends call, don’t want to leave the house.  

I don’t care about the awards I used to win or new projects. I feel slow, like my body’s made of stone. Some days, standing near the balcony, I get this sudden urge to step forward—no plan, just… impulse. Like it’d make all the thoughts stop. I don’t think I’d actually do it, but the thought scares me.  

I feel useless, like I’ve become a shell. The sadness and the odd thoughts? They’ve been here the whole time—mixed together, really. I can’t tell where one ends and the other begins.
D007-D005_h013.options:
A. Anorexia Nervosa
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    D. Schizophrenia
D007-D005_h013.answer: B & D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type) & Schizophrenia

D007-D005_h014.question:
I’ve been struggling for about seven months now—maybe longer, it’s hard to tell. At work, the voices started—clear as you are—telling me I’m chosen, that I can see things others can't. They say I’m connected to a higher system, like I was born to protect something big. I sometimes hear them rhyming—“signs align, divine design”—it sticks in my head. I’ll stand in place for minutes, sometimes hours, just holding my arms up like I’m on duty, even when I’m off the clock. My wife says I don’t talk much anymore, that my voice is flat, like I don’t care, but it's not that. I just… feel heavy.  

I don’t see my friends. Don’t answer the phone. What’s the point? I’ve let things go. I used to take pride in being dependable—18 years in security, never missed a shift—but now I sit in the dark. I think about not waking up. Wouldn’t be a loss, really. The voices still tell me I’m important, but honestly, I feel worthless. I can’t sleep, but when I do, it’s like I’m not even there. Everything’s slowed down. I’m just… waiting.
D007-D005_h014.options:
A. Anorexia Nervosa
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    D. Schizophrenia
D007-D005_h014.answer: B & D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type) & Schizophrenia

D007-D005_h015.question:
I’ve been struggling for about seven months now—some days are worse than others. Since my husband passed, the bakery’s been closed. I used to love decorating cakes, especially for weddings, but now… I can’t even bring myself to turn on the ovens. I don’t care about anything anymore, and I feel so slow, like my body’s made of lead. Walking to the mailbox takes effort. I keep thinking it’s my fault things fell apart—that if I’d been a better wife, a better person, he’d still be here. Sometimes I think… I know how it could end. There’s a bridge near the old flour mill. I could just walk out to the middle late at night when no one’s around.

But it’s not just sadness. I see things. My late husband, standing in the kitchen in his apron, smiling at me. He doesn’t speak, just watches. And there’s this man—I don’t know him, but I know he loves me. He’s handsome, foreign—comes into the bakery in my mind. He sends signals, I’m sure of it. The radio playing “Unchained Melody” the other day? That was for me.

I catch myself laughing for no reason, like a little girl, then crying a minute later. People say I mumble, that what I say doesn’t make sense. I don’t feel much—my face, I’m told, doesn’t move like it used to.
D007-D005_h015.options:
A. Anorexia Nervosa
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    D. Schizophrenia
D007-D005_h015.answer: B & D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type) & Schizophrenia

D007-D005_h016.question:
I’ve been struggling for nearly a year, maybe longer. At first, it was just the weight—I lost over 20 pounds without trying, and clothes hang off me now. I’m so tired all the time; even opening mail feels like climbing a hill. I don’t care about anything anymore—work, home, my husband—it’s like I’m watching my life from far away, numb, empty. I cry sometimes, but it feels automatic, not real.

About eight months ago, things got… strange. I started noticing patterns—in the way people on the street look at me, or how coworkers phrase things. I know it sounds odd, but I’m convinced the news anchors tailor their words to me during the evening broadcast. Once, I saw my late father standing by my car, but when I got closer, he wasn’t there. I’ve seen shadows like that since, fleeting—figures in my periphery that vanish.

I used to be on top of everything—budgets, staff, clients. Now I can’t make myself start tasks. I sit at my desk and nothing moves. I still show up, but I’m falling behind. My husband says I’ve changed, and I believe him. I just don’t know how much of this is sadness… or something else. The lines between what’s real and what’s not feel thin—especially at night, when the dreams are so vivid and dark I dread closing my eyes.
D007-D005_h016.options:
A. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    D. Body Dysmorphic Disorder
D007-D005_h016.answer: C & B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type) & Schizophrenia

D007-D005_h017.question:
I’ve been struggling for about a year now—maybe a bit more. At first, it was just the insomnia. I’d wake around 3 a.m. and just lie there, staring at the ceiling, mentally exhausted even though I hadn’t done anything. My thoughts feel heavy, like pushing through mud. I used to be on top of everything at the hospital—now I can’t even bring myself to organize my schedule. I’ve lost interest in most things, even things I used to enjoy with my husband.

I’ve dropped nearly 15 pounds without trying, just from not being hungry. There’s a constant emptiness, like I’m just going through the motions. At work, I’ve started noticing things—staff whispering in the hall, and I know they’re talking about me. Not just gossip—important messages about me being hidden in routine announcements. Once, I felt something crawling under my skin, like insects beneath the surface. I checked but there was nothing. It happens when I’m stressed, like the walls are closing in.

These episodes come and go. I can’t tell if the low mood came first, or if the strange thoughts pulled me down. I just know I can’t function like I used to. But I can’t say which part is driving the other—I just feel caught in the middle.
D007-D005_h017.options:
A. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    D. Body Dysmorphic Disorder
D007-D005_h017.answer: C & B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type) & Schizophrenia

D007-D005_h018.question:
I’ve been struggling for about eight or nine months—maybe closer to a year now—just feeling… off. Work has gotten harder, even though I used to thrive on the structure. I’m an IT project manager, so communication is key, but lately I’ve found myself saying less and less in meetings. It’s not that I don’t have thoughts—I do—but it’s like the words won’t come out. My team’s noticed.  

I’ve been hearing things, too. Voices. Not all the time, but enough. Mostly whispering my name or saying I’m being betrayed. That part… it’s about my girlfriend. I know she says she’s loyal, but I *know*—I can *feel* it—she’s seeing someone else. She stays late “working,” but I hear the tone in her voice when she texts. The voices confirm it.  

I can’t sleep. I lie there for hours, exhausted but wired. When I do sleep, I wake up drained. I’ve lost weight—maybe 10 pounds—just from not eating. Food tastes like nothing. Some days, getting out of bed takes everything I have. I used to run; now walking to the kitchen feels heavy.  

I don’t know if it’s the stress or something deeper. It’s all mixed together—my mind, my mood, what I hear. Hard to tell what’s real anymore.
D007-D005_h018.options:
A. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    D. Body Dysmorphic Disorder
D007-D005_h018.answer: C & B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type) & Schizophrenia

D007-D005_h019.question:
I’ve been having a hard time for about a year now—maybe longer. Lately, nothing feels real. I don’t cry, but I don’t feel anything either, not even when my grandson calls. Some days, I just sit on the edge of the bed, too tired to move, even after sleeping. Falling asleep is hard—my mind just won’t shut off, even if my body’s exhausted. I eat more than I used to, mindlessly—cleaning the fridge, then opening snack bags just to keep my hands busy.  

At work, I keep thinking people are talking about me. Not loud, but in whispers, or laughing when someone drops a rag—like it’s a signal. Once, a guest said “it stinks in here,” and I knew they meant me, even though the trash was full. Sometimes, I smell burning hair in empty rooms. I’ve checked the stove twice. Nothing.  

I don’t say much anymore. Hard to start a sentence. My coworker asks how I am, and I just nod. Why talk if they already know what you’re thinking? I’ve missed shifts—I can’t face the bus, the noise, the looks. I used to pride myself on not missing work. Now, I wonder if I should just stop.  

It’s been like this for months—long enough that I don’t know which thoughts are mine and which aren’t.
D007-D005_h019.options:
A. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    D. Body Dysmorphic Disorder
D007-D005_h019.answer: C & B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type) & Schizophrenia

D007-D005_h020.question:
I’ve been feeling off for nearly a year now—maybe longer. Lately, I wake up in the middle of the night and can’t get back to sleep, no matter how tired I am. I used to enjoy dinner with my wife, but now I barely eat; food just doesn’t interest me. I cry sometimes for no reason—just sitting in the dark, feeling empty. I’ve lost a lot of weight, and I’m always drained, even after a full night’s rest.  

At work, I keep to myself. I used to chat with the crew, but now I don’t see the point. Something just feels… disconnected. But it’s not just that.
